Cancel {/* "Edit Invoice" in the edit forms */}

That is as clean an extraction as this detector will ever hand you. ## Scope constraint worth stating up front `final-example` and `starter-example` are **two independent Next.js apps** — separate `package.json`, and each `tsconfig.json` maps `@/*` → `./*` within its own root. There is no workspace linking them, so a single component file cannot serve all four call sites without introducing a shared package, which would restructure a tutorial fixture whose whole point is that the two copies stand alone. So: **extract twice, once per app.** Each extraction removes 2 of the 4 occurrences. That is the correct read of this finding — 4 occurrences, 2 real refactors, not 1. ## Proposed shared component **New file (×2):** - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/form-actions.tsx` - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/form-actions.tsx` ### Public API ```tsx import Link from 'next/link'; import { Button } from '@/app/ui/button'; export interface InvoiceFormActionsProps { /** Submit button label — the only thing that varies today. */ submitLabel: string; /** Where Cancel navigates. Defaults to the invoices index. */ cancelHref?: string; /** Cancel link text. */ cancelLabel?: string; /** Disables submit; forwarded to
); } ``` **Props:** `submitLabel` (required — the one real variant), `cancelHref` / `cancelLabel` (defaulted, so no call site passes them today), `disabled` (forward-looking; `Button` extends `React.ButtonHTMLAttributes` and spreads `...rest`, so it passes through with no change to `button.tsx`). **Slots:** one — `children`, rendered leading, for a future destructive or secondary action. Deliberately *not* slots for cancel or submit: making those slots would let the two forms drift again, which is the exact failure this extraction is closing. `submitLabel` as a string, not a node, keeps the contract narrow. Only `submitLabel` is required, so both call sites collapse to a single line and there is no configuration surface to get wrong. ### Call sites ```tsx // create-form.tsx // edit-form.tsx ``` ## Files that change **New (2):** - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/form-actions.tsx` - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/form-actions.tsx` **Modified (4)** — each loses a 9-line subtree, drops its now-unused `Link` and `Button` imports, and gains one import: - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` (142–150; drop `Link` L4, `Button` L11) - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` (152–160; drop `Link` L10, `Button` L11) - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` (101–109) - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` (112–120) Verify the `Link`/`Button` imports are genuinely unused before deleting them — in these four files they are, but that is a per-file check, not an assumption to carry. No tests exist for these components (`test_gap: 0.5`, `blast_radius: 0` — nothing imports the forms but the route pages). The refactor is behaviour-preserving markup movement; risk is that the rendered DOM must be identical, which a snapshot of the action bar would pin if you want one. ## What this deliberately does not fix The action bar is the smallest duplication in these files, not the largest. The same scan shows the *rest* of create-form and edit-form is near-duplicate too — the customer `` block, and the status `
` are structurally the same in both forms of each app, with the edit form adding `defaultValue` / `defaultChecked`. Corroborating findings on the same four files: - `crime_00006` — the `"status"` literal across all four forms plus `actions.ts:43` - `crime_00065` / `crime_00066` — `"paid"` and `"pending"` compared in 4 files across 2 expression shapes, edit-form and `status.tsx` disagreeing - `crime_00072` / `crime_00073` / `crime_00076` / `crime_00077` — the same 5 hard-coded `px` values (`18px`, `18px`, `18px`, `18px`, `14px`) in all four forms Those point at a fuller extraction — an `InvoiceFormFields` component plus a status constant — which is a larger, riskier change with real API design questions (how the edit form seeds defaults).
